subject.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks

question: Which open implementation should be canonical for the global-breaker reachability bug: this typed `loop-veto` outcome branch or the sentinel-hash branch at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619?
rationale: Both branches close the same open issue but encode the invariant differently; choosing the durable session-record contract is an owner decision before a merge can safely proceed.

options.title: Land the typed-outcome branch
options.body: Use this PR’s explicit `loop-veto` outcome because it preserves the distinction between detector vetoes and ordinary result hashes while allowing progress to reset an older stalled segment.

options.title: Land the sentinel-hash branch
options.body: Choose https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619 if maintainers prefer its narrower hash-based representation, then close this competing branch.

options.title: Pause both implementations
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and request a single maintainer-authored resolution if neither representation matches the desired long-term diagnostics contract.

recommendation.title: Land the typed-outcome branch
recommendation.body: Use this PR’s explicit `loop-veto` outcome because it preserves the distinction between detector vetoes and ordinary result hashes while allowing progress to reset an older stalled segment.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current loop-veto invariant in the merged loop-detection history and are the strongest available owner for selecting its durable representation.
